rationale: A wins because it mostly stays inside the facts and turns the thin update into four usable reporting paths. Its strongest line, "Linear is expanding into a new buyer segment with no enterprise sales team in sight," is cautious enough to demand proof instead of pretending the proof exists. B has sharper teeth, but "Linear opens the product-management market it spent years refusing to enter" invents company history in the headline, which is how a pitch walks itself into traffic.
gaps_in_A: "The prevailing playbook says moving into a new function — here, product and design, historically sold top-down to VPs — requires a sales-led motion" adds market context that is plausible but not supplied; it needs to be framed as a question, not a given.

"Another roadmapping tool arrives for product teams already drowning in software" imports a tooling-fatigue trend without evidence from the update. The proof section admits the gap, but the headline is still doing extra work.
"Decay: 24hr" on the GTM angle is too cramped. The launch is same-day, but the self-serve-versus-sales question can live for several days if Linear gives an executive answer.

The competitive angle is useful but underpowered until it names the category evidence it lacks; "product-management turf" is fine color, but the update gives no competitors, market data, or replacement claim.
gaps_in_B: "spent years refusing to enter" is invented. The update says Linear is expanding beyond engineering now; it does not say the company refused this market for years.
"the Jira/Asana/Notion competitive set" smuggles in named competitors, then the refused angles scold "Linear takes on Jira" as hallucinated. Pick a standard and live by it.
"Stakeholder views are, by definition, for people who open the tool weekly, not hourly" is a confident stereotype, not a supplied fact. It may be true in some teams; it is not evidence.

"what product managers actually lose when their roadmap lives outside the engineers' tool" assumes a split-stack pain story the update does not document. B correctly asks for a named PM later, but the angle headline gets ahead of the proof.
